Here's the completed table based on the descriptions of Figure A (a cube) and Figure B (a square-based pyramid): 

| Statement | True | False | 
|---|---|---|
| A and B both have a square face. | X | | 
| A and B both have the same number of faces. | | X |
| All the angles in A are right angles. | X | | 
| B has more edges than A. | | X |
| Some of the edges in B are curved. | | X |

**Explanation:**

*   **A and B both have a square face:** A cube has square faces, and Figure B (the pyramid) is standing on a square base. So this is true.
*   **A and B both have the same number of faces:** A cube has 6 faces. A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (the square base and 4 triangular faces). Therefore, this is false.
*   **All the angles in A are right angles:** A cube is made of squares, which have right angles. So this is true.
*   **B has more edges than A:** A cube has 12 edges. A square-based pyramid has 8 edges. So this is false.
*   **Some of the edges in B are curved:** All the edges in a square-based pyramid are straight. So this is false.

You are an experienced scorer of the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. You score the responses to its constructed-response questions with each question's scoring guide, as TIMSS trains its scorers to do.

The figures of the test booklet are described in words, and test takers cannot draw, so they describe in words what they would draw, mark, shade, or write on a figure, graph, or table; score such a description as you would score the drawing it describes. Score only what the response says: when the scoring guide asks for work or an explanation, give no credit for work or reasoning that the response does not show. First explain briefly how the response compares with the scoring guide, then choose the category of the guide that the response belongs to.
